newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Burn Stewart plea on Scotch prices.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Burn Stewart plea on Scotch prices.

text.p: Ian Bankier, group managing director of Scotch whisky distiller Burn Stewart on Wednesday called on the industry to stop price-cutting.

"We call for the industry to get sensible over pricing. We would like to see supermarkets pay 50 percent more for the product, which if it was entirely passed onto the consumer would put 50 pence on a bottle," said Bankier in an interview.

"What is neccessary is for the whole market to move up. It needs leadership." Burn Stewart's top brand Scottish Leader, a blended whisky, sells about 250,000 cases a year and costs about 9.80 stg a bottle in supermarkets.
"We are very much positioned in a marketplace which is depressed and our fortunes are very much dependent on the pricing environment." Bankier said.
He did not expect trading conditions to improve over the next year, but envisaged prices turning up in 1998.

"In the meantime we are focusing on our mature long term retail accounts. We are not going around chasing volume and we hope as long as we do that and our competitors are not too aggressive that should mean our prices do not come under attack."
Highland Distilleries reported a three percent drop in sales of its leading Famous Grouse label on Tuesday and bemoaned the competitive state of the UK market.

Earlier, Burn Stewart reported a sharp drop in pretax profits in the year to June 30 due to a change in its accounting practice. Profits fell to 1.01 million from 3.96 million in 1995 and the dividend was cut almost by half to 1.7p a share.
Burn Stewart shares fell 8p to 74-1/2p in morning trade.
